cards.explanation: The answer is Aaron and his sons. The LORD tells Moses, "Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites." (Numbers 6:23) Moses is the middleman here, and Aaron and his sons are the ones who get the words to say. The blessing itself is for the Israelites. Passing along a message without changing a word is a real skill, friends, and I've seen people mess up a simple grocery list.

The answer is to speak them to the people. God's instruction is "Say to them…" and then He gives the words. (Numbers 6:23) So this blessing is meant to be spoken out loud, friends. No paperwork, no engraving, just Aaron and his sons saying it to the Israelites.

The answer is that the LORD may be gracious to them. Line two says, "…may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you…" (Numbers 6:25) The shining face and the grace come together in one line, friends. I think that's a warm thing to hear spoken over you.

The answer is True. Look at the verbs, friends: "May the LORD bless you and keep you…" then "…may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you…" then "…may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and give you peace." (Numbers 6:24-26) Every line starts with the LORD and what He does. The blessing is all about Him giving.

The answer is His name. God says, "So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them." (Numbers 6:27) When Aaron and his sons speak the blessing, they're putting God's name on His people, friends. It's a big moment, and it happens just by speaking the words.

The answer is False. Aaron and his sons speak the words and put God's name on the Israelites, but God says, "…I will bless them." (Numbers 6:27) The priests are the ones who say the blessing, friends, and God is the One who says He will bless His people.
